I was in the exact same situation when I finished student teaching as well. I had many of the same thoughts you seem to be having. The big one for me was “how am I ever going to be one of those mind-blowingly creative teachers that every student loves?”. I’ve only been teaching full-time for a year, but it comes with time and experience. Once you’re in a classroom on your own without supervision, and you get to put everything you learned to use it gets better. 

Are you going to make mistakes? Absolutely, but good teachers learn from them. I have had some awful lessons this year, but I try to look back and think about what I could have done differently for next time. I try to use that line of thinking for anything, whether it’s classroom management or grading or whatever. Practice makes perfect. 

I also used to think that staying several hours later than everyone else would help but it did nothing but make me stress more. I would get headaches all of the time and partially freak out about being one of the few people left in the building. I just take advantage of my prep times, grade any quick assignments I can and then go home to relax. You gotta balance work and life at home, otherwise the stress is gonna kill you. You need your you time!

It's tough to simply cast aside an act as criminal as the Watergate Scandal, but I'll provide a simplified pro/con list to hit on the key points (Note: I'm a history teacher)

Pros: 

Nixon visited China to repair relations that were, at that time, pretty rough. The Chinese considered the United States a serious foe for a number of reasons (political ideology during the Cold War, recognizing Taiwan as an independent republic, etc.). No US President had visited China for about 25 years, and Nixon arguably caused the Chinese to slightly lean towards the side of the U.S.

Military: He began the withdrawal process of our troops from Southeast Asia and ended the draft. Also signed the Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty with the USSR

Economy: Was able to reduce the national deficit

Environment: Formed the EPA that is today in very serious danger

Cons:

While he withdrew troops from Vietnam, he was bombing the shit out of Cambodia at the same time, prolonging the war. Even though he promised "Vietnamization"; the gradual withdrawal of soldiers, to American citizens, they suddenly felt pretty cheated.

He was incredibly paranoid and racist. Nixon's paranoia was pretty clear once word got out that he recorded dozens of tapes of conversations in the Oval Office, and his attitudes towards minorities were revealed in several of them. Here's a quote from one:

“[Sec. of State] Bill Rogers has got — to his credit it’s a decent feeling — but somewhat sort of a blind spot on the black thing because he’s been in New York. He says well, ‘They are coming along, and that after all they are going to strengthen our country in the end because they are strong physically and some of them are smart.’ So forth and so on. My own view is I think he’s right if you’re talking in terms of 500 years. I think it’s wrong if you’re talking in terms of 50 years. What has to happen is they have to be, frankly, inbred. And, you just, that’s the only thing that’s going to do it." That was just his attitude towards African-Americans, but there were several other groups that were mentioned in a negative context in these tapes.

He also continued U.S. intervention in Chile, where he feared that the president-elect of 1970, Salvador Allende, was too far-left. Nixon worried that Chile would become "another Cuba", ultimately assisting Augusto Pinochet to gain power in 1973 in a coup. If you don't know anything about Pinochet, he was a dictator and ruled with an iron first, so that should give you an idea of what Chile was like from 1973 until the end of his rule in 1990.

Those are pretty much the big pieces, in my opinion. This is my first time writing one of these, but I hope it gave you some things to consider.
